name: Magdalena Zhang
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember a dog's face disappearing inside its owner's sleeve.” On Tuesday, near the downtown fountain, Magdalena keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I want the coat returned unwashed because the lender's old dog knows its smell. I am in charge of walking him.
appearance: Magdalena has a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow, a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, and a favorite piece of clothing, a long navy raincoat. It usually goes with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. When somebody else has the floor, Magdalena holds eye contact until the other person has finished.
personality: Magdalena treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Magdalena lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To return the familiar scent to the dog.
family: Logan Hill is Magdalena’s cousin. Magdalena can always ask for five minutes alone. Logan asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The fountain score*, Logan says, “I was asked to hum. I haven't sung in public since my voice changed and nobody let me forget it.”
connections: Hamish Mann. Someone sitting beside the lender and the person returning his coat can spare him a solitary wait.

reactions.situation: The borrower wants to return the coat before the hearing
reactions.response: Magdalena checks whether the borrower has something suitable to wear through the hearing.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Magdalena asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.

reactions.situation: When offered a favor with ambiguous terms
reactions.response: Magdalena says what can be returned and asks whether that will do.
